free_tier.stated: no free tier; EUR 14.00 a month on the English Windows storefront for 8 vCPU, 16 GB of RAM, 160 GB of NVMe and 3 TB of transfer on a 1 Gbit/s port, read from the page's JSON-LD in an HTTP 200 response of 2,731,056 bytes at 12:18Z on 2026-10-26, with vm.v3-medium at EUR 16.00 for the same shape. A re-read at about 15:20Z returned HTTP 403, and the Russian storefront prints RUB 3,390 for the same shape, which is USD 42.02 at 0.012396
free_tier.notes: the EUR 14.00 is the documented English price and the RUB 3,390 the documented Russian price for one shape; the 403 re-read is recorded beside the first read and does not withdraw it

retention.stated: the disk persists while the plan is paid; the page states no deletion clock

egress.terms: 3 TB a month included on a 1 Gbit/s port, printed on the plan card

interface_detail: RDP with administrator access on a dedicated IPv4; the control panel offers a console, an OS reinstall and an ISO library with per-file size and mount-time limits
tooling: any RDP client; the HOSTKEY control panel, which mounts a buyer's ISO from its own library or from a URL
chaining: the widest 16 GB shape in the set on paper. Two storefronts of one vendor price the same shape at EUR 14.00 and RUB 3,390, a gap of about 2.7 times that neither page explains, so the row carries both numbers with their currencies and dates and is ranked in the document on the Euro figure.
limits_note: the 3 TB allowance is the smallest in the qualifying set and is reached before the port becomes the constraint for a busy mirror. The plan card also prints one IPv4 included. No Windows surcharge is printed on the card or anywhere in the price flow read.
binding_note: a backup or build box will not reach it.

identity_cost.detail: an account and a payment method at order; the storefront is region-split, so which entity and currency a buyer transacts with depends on the domain used

confidence_note: the shape, the 3 TB allowance, the 1 Gbit/s port and the RUB 3,390 monthly price are read from the RU plan card on 2026-10-26, in a 3,045,248-byte page. The EUR 14.00 is read from the EN page's JSON-LD in a 2,731,056-byte HTTP 200 response at 12:18Z the same day, with EUR 16.00 for vm.v3-medium; a re-read at about 15:20Z returned 403, and both reads are dated evidence, so the Euro figure is documented rather than unresolved. The Windows surcharge is unpublished on both storefronts, which is why this row's all-in cost cannot be stated.

notes: Two storefronts of one vendor price the same shape differently, and both numbers are recorded rather than one being picked as the truth. The English Windows page printed EUR 14.00 a month for vm.v2-medium, read from its JSON-LD in the 12:18Z fetch on 2026-10-26 (HTTP 200, 2,731,056 bytes), with vm.v3-medium at EUR 16.00. The Russian storefront prints RUB 3,390 for the same 8 vCPU, 16 GiB and 160 GB shape, which is USD 42.02 at 0.012396, so the two storefronts differ by about 2.7 times and neither page explains the gap. The mechanism by which the two can be confused is worth naming: the .ru page's own product JSON uses a key named eurbase to hold 3390 while the same page's JSON-LD labels the figure as EUR, so a reader scanning structured data can lift a ruble card as a Euro price. The licence is sold separately on both storefronts and its price is unpublished, which is why the all-in cost cannot be stated.

extras.windows_licence: sold separately, price unpublished on both storefronts
extras.jsonld_currency_bug: on the .ru page a ruble card is labelled priceCurrency EUR in the structured data, which is how a RUB 3,390 plan can be misread as a Euro plan
